item.title: SNAPSHOT | Red Dragons look ahead to FA Cup Fourth Round
item.description: Attention turned to a Friday night FA Cup tie under the lights against Ipswich Town this week, at Wrexham AFC’s first-team training. Ahead of the first of two games against the Tractor Boys in the space of eight days, the Red Dragons were without Matty James and Libby Cacace at Colliers Park but otherwise at full strength. item.description: Manager Phil Parkinson is relishing another night under the STōK Cae Ras floodlights, as the Red Dragons prepare to welcome Ipswich Town in the FA Cup Fourth Round. item.title: COMMUNITY | Wrexham AFC Foundation partner with The Waterloo Foundation
item.description: Wrexham AFC Foundation are delighted to announce a new three-year strategic partnership with The Waterloo Foundation. This exciting partnership is designed to strengthen and expand the Club’s Young Leaders programmes, ensuring it reaches more young people across North Wales and delivers lasting benefits for individuals and their communities. item.title: FIXTURE NEWS | Wrexham AFC vs Swansea City FC selected for live TV coverage
item.description: Our Sky Bet Championship home fixture against Swansea City at the STōK Cae Ras, will now kick off on Friday March 13 at 8pm, having been selected for live TV coverage on Sky Sports Football. item.title: REPORT | Wrexham AFC 1-0 Ipswich Town (FA Cup)
item.description: Wrexham AFC booked their place in the Fifth Round of the FA Cup, as Josh Windass’ 34th minute strike earned the Red Dragons a 1-0 victory over Ipswich Town. Goalkeeper Alex Palmer was called into action early-on, but chances were few and far between before Windass broke the deadlock 11 minutes prior to the interval. item.title: GALLERY | Wrexham AFC 1-0 Ipswich Town
item.description: Wrexham AFC put themselves into the hat for the FA Cup Fifth Round for the first time since 1997 with victory over visiting Ipswich Town. Phil Parkinson made five changes to his starting XI, including a return for Ryan Longman and Josh Windass, as well as Sam Smith, George Dobson and George Thomason. item.title: U18 REPORT | Wrexham AFC 0-1 Port Vale
item.description: Wrexham AFC Under-18s suffered their first defeat of 2026, as they lost 1-0 at home to Port Vale. It means their six-match unbeaten run has come to an end, having secured wins over Shrewsbury Town, Morecambe, Southend United, and Walsall, and drawn with Oldham Athletic and Blackpool.
